name: Maya Ellison
text: Ran a half marathon in them in week three with no hot spots. The rocker takes a couple of runs to trust, then you stop noticing it.

name: Diego Ruiz
text: Lighter than my old daily trainer and the heel counter actually holds. The clay is warmer in person than in photos.

name: Naomi Clarke
text: Wore them for two ten-hour shifts on a hospital ward. My feet were tired, not sore, which is a first.

name: Peter Wong
text: Snug for the first week, then the knit relaxed. Glad I followed the advice and stayed in my usual size.

name: Isaac Bell
text: Went half a size down as the page suggested and it was right. Heel lockdown is excellent for pickup.

name: Colin Reyes
text: The forest suede is a deep, proper green. Grip on our dusty community court is far better than my old pair.

name: Lena Park
text: The strap makes them feel secure in dance class without being stiff. Took about a week to soften.

name: Victor Lang
text: Sharp with wide trousers. The leather creased a little at the toe, which I expected.

name: Ada Okafor
text: Took them on the canal towpath in the rain and my feet stayed dry. Sized up half as advised for thick socks.

name: Felix Grant
text: Grippy on gravel and not clunky on the road to get there. The toggle laces are quicker than I expected.

name: Tessa Hart
text: Stable enough for deadlifts, soft enough for the 2 km warm-up. The wide toe box suits my feet.

name: Omar Haidar
text: Burpees wore through my last pair in four months. These look barely touched after the same.

name: Imani Brooks
text: Wore them on a four-day city trip, about 60 km in total. The suede still looks new after a brush.

name: Rosa Vega
text: Ordered two sizes, kept the 9.5 and sent the 9 back with the label in the box. No questions asked.

name: June Alvarez
text: My Everyday Arcs came back from resoling looking like a new pair for ₹3,499. Bought a second pair anyway.

name: Kenji Mori
text: Runs large like they say. Half a size down was perfect, and the gum sole flexes straight out of the box.
